sections.name: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR

items.label: Required Upper-Division
items.notes: *If both ECE 153A and ECE 153B are taken, one may be used as a departmental elective and the other will be used as a required course.

items.label: Approved Departmental Electives
items.description: Approval of the student’s departmental electives must be obtained from the student’s faculty adviser. The departmental electives must include an approved depth sequence corresponding to the students’ chosen track, or another depth sequence of at least 4 courses that is approved by the students’ faculty advisor. See the ECE Department Student Office for the list of courses in the different areas of specialization.
items.notes:
- ECE 194AA-ZZ (excluding ECE 194R)
- ECE 192 or 196 (4 units combined max)
- TMP 120, 122 (1 course max)

sections.notes: To satisfy major requirements, courses taken inside or outside the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, must be taken for a letter grade.

nodes.title: General Chemistry
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.description: Topics covered: atomic structure of matter; reaction stoichiometry; solution stoichiometry; gasses; quantum chemistry and the electronic structure of atoms; chemical bonding (molecular shapes, hybridization, and molecular orbital theory).

nodes.title: General Chemistry
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 1A, CHEM 2A or CHEM 3A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Topics covered: equilibrium; acids, bases, and buffers; thermochemistry (energy, enthalpy, entropy, and free energy); electrochemistry.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Honors)
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.description: The sequence of topics will be similar to that in Chemistry 1A. Calculus will be used as needed, at the level of the concurrent Mathematics 3A course.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Majors)
nodes.prereq_text: None
nodes.description: Topics covered: atomic structure of matter; reaction stoichiometry; solution stoichiometry; gasses; quantum chemistry and the electronic structure of atoms; chemical bonding (molecular shapes, hybridization, and molecular orbital theory). First quarter of general chemistry intended for Chemistry Pre-Majors and Chemical Engineering Majors and others requiring a strong basis in chemistry.

nodes.title: Introduction to Computer Science
nodes.description: Introduction to computer program development for students with little to no programming experience. Basic programming concepts, variables and expressions, data and control structures, algorithms, debugging, program design, and documentation.

nodes.title: Intermediate Python Programming
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: CMPSC 8 or CMPSC W8 or ENGR 3 or ENGR W3 or ECE 3 with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Intermediate topics in Computer Science using the Python programming language. Topics include object oriented programming, runtime analysis, data structures, and software testing methodologies.

nodes.title: Problem Solving with Computers I
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 3A or 2A with a grade of C or better (may be taken concurrently), CS 8 or Engineering 3 or ECE 3 with a grade of C or better, or significant prior programming experience.

items.text: significant prior programming experience

nodes.description: Fundamental building blocks for solving problems using computers. Topics include basic computer organization and programming constructs: memory CPU, binary arithmetic, variables, expressions, statements, conditionals, iteration, functions, parameters, recursion, primitive and composite data types, and basic operating system and debugging tools.

nodes.title: Problem Solving with Computers II
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 16 with a grade of C or better; and Mathematics 3B or 2B with a grade of C or better (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Intermediate building blocks for solving problems using computers. Topics include intermediate object-oriented programming, data structures, object-oriented design, algorithms for manipulating these data structures and their run-time analyses. Data structures introduced include stacks, queues, lists, trees, and sets.

nodes.title: Data Programming and Analytics for Artificial Intelligence
nodes.prereq_text: CMPSC 9 or CMPSC 24 with a grade of C or better; and, Mathematics 3A or 2A with a grade of C or better (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Course delves into essential programming, algorithmic, and data analytics techniques foundational to artificial intelligence. Topics include data acquisition, cleaning, transformation, modeling, sampling, visualization and simulation, statistical programming, hypothesis testing, inference, with applications in artificial intelligence. Students will apply these concepts through hands-on Python projects, gaining practical experience in using data analytics to develop intelligent systems.

nodes.title: Foundations of Computer Science
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 16 with a grade of C or better and Mathematics 4A with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Introduction to the theoretical underpinnings of computer science. Topics include propositional predicate logic, set theory, functions and relations, counting, mathematical induction and recursion (generating functions).

nodes.title: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 16 with a grade of C or better and Mathematics 4A with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Introductory discrete mathematics. Topics include fundamental principles of counting (permutations, combinations), sets, graph theory, elementary probability, and number theory.

nodes.title: Computer Organization and Logic Design
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 16 with a grade of C or better; and Mathematics 3C or 4A with a grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Assembly language programming and advanced computer organization; digital logic design topics including gates, combinational circuits, flip-flops, and the design and analysis of sequential circuits.

nodes.title: Data Structures and Algorithms
nodes.prereq_text: CMPSC 40 or CMPSC 41 or MATH 8 with a grade of C or better; CMPSC 24 or CMPSC 25 with a grade of C or better; PSTAT 120A or ECE 139 (may be taken concurrently with CMPSC 130A); open to Computer Science Department majors, and Electrical and Computer Engineering Department majors only.

items.text: open to Computer Science Department majors, and Electrical and Computer Engineering Department majors only

nodes.description: Data structures and applications with proofs of correctness and analysis. Hash Tables, Priority Queues (heaps); Balanced Search Trees. Graph Traversal techniques and their applications.

nodes.title: Algorithm Design and Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Computer Science 130A.
nodes.description: Design and analysis of computer algorithms. Correctness proofs and solution of recurrence relations. Design techniques; divide and conquer, greedy strategies, dynamic programming. Applications of techniques to problems from several disciplines. NP - completeness.

nodes.title: Introduction to Computer Science
nodes.description: Introduction to computer program development for students with little to no programming experience. Basic programming concepts, variables and expressions, data and control structures, algorithms, debugging, program design, and documentation.

nodes.title: Introduction to Python Programming For Engineers
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: Open to EE and CMPEN majors only.

requires.text: Open to EE and CMPEN majors only

nodes.description: This course represents a comprehensive foundation for core ECE topics in signal processing, image analysis, machine learning, optimization and control. The lectures present concepts from linear algebra, such as matrix computations, systems of linear equations, eigenspace decomposition, inner-product, orthogonality, least-squares and linear regression. Students actively engage with the technical materials with an introduction to Python programming and associated hands-on sessions. The materials are be motivated by real-world scenarios ranging from medical imaging to autonomous vehicles, from (miscarriage of) justice to brain-machine interfaces, from music analysis to GPS design.

nodes.title: Introduction to Electrical & Computer Engineering
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: Open only to Electrical Engineering and Computer Engineering majors.

requires.text: Open only to Electrical Engineering and Computer Engineering majors

nodes.description: Aims at exposing freshmen students to the different sub-fields within Electrical and Computer Engineering. Composed of lectures by different faculty members and a weekly laboratory based on projects that are executed using the Arduino environment.

nodes.title: The Physics of Energy, Information, and Communication
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: Open to Electrical Engineering majors only.

requires.text: Open to Electrical Engineering majors only

nodes.description: An introduction to the relationship between the physical nature of matter and modern problems in energy harvesting, energy storage, information storage, and communication. Key emphasis is placed on understanding materials and how materials are used to make functional electronics and photonics. The primary outcome of this course is to enable students to understand the relevance of later Physics, Math, and E&P courses with real-world examples and investigations.

nodes.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits & Systems
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or Mathematics 3AH-BH, and Mathematics 4A or 4AI or 3C, all with a minimum grade of C; and, Math 4B or 4BI or 5A with a minimum grade of C (may be taken concurrently); Physics 3, 7B or 23 (may be taken concurrently); open only to electrical engineering and computer engineering majors.

items.text: open only to electrical engineering and computer engineering majors

nodes.description: The objective of the course is to establish the foundations of analog and digital circuits. The course will introduce the student to the power of abstraction, resistive networks, network analysis, nonlinear analysis and the digital abstraction.

nodes.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits and Systems Lab
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 10A (may be taken concurrently) with a C- or better grade.
nodes.description: The goal of 10AL is to provide the student with a hands-on application of the concepts discussed in ECE 10A. The lab will introduce the use of microcontrollers as a data acquisition system, network analysis, resistors, nonlinear analysis and digital abstraction.

nodes.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits and Systems
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 10A with a C- or better grade.
nodes.description: The objective of the course is to introduce the MOSFET both as a simple digital switch and as controlled current source for analog design. The course will cover basic digital design, small-signal analysis, charge storage elements and operational amplifiers.

nodes.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits and Systems Lab
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 10B (may be taken concurrently) with a C- or better grade.
nodes.description: The goal of 10BL is to provide the student with a hands-on application of the concepts discussed in ECE 10B. The lab will utilize the microcontroller to introduce students to the understanding of datasheets for both digital and analog circuits, single-stage amplifier design and basic instrumentation.

nodes.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits and Systems
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 10B with a C- or better grade.
nodes.description: The objective of the course is to introduce the student to the basics of transient analysis. The course will energy and power dissipation in digital circuits, first-order and second-order linear time invariant circuits, sinusoidal steady state, impedance representation, feedback and resonance.

nodes.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits and Systems Lab
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 10C (may be taken concurrently) with a C- grade or better.
nodes.description: The goal of 10CL is to provide the student with a hands-on application of the concepts discussed in ECE 10C. The lab will utilize the microcontroller to introduce students to the understanding of propagation delay in digital circuits and the resulting power dissipation, first order linear networks, second order linear networks, sinusoidal steady-state, impedance analysis and op-amp circuits.

nodes.title: Fundamentals of Logic Design
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: Open to electrical engineering, computer engineering, and pre-computer engineering majors only.

requires.text: Open to electrical engineering, computer engineering, and pre-computer engineering majors only

nodes.description: Boolean algebra, logic of propositions, minterm and maxterm expansions, Karnaugh maps, Quine-McCluskey method, melti-level circuits, combinational circuit design and simulation, multiplexers, decoders, programmable logic devices.

nodes.title: Integrated Circuit Design and Fabrication
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 132 with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Theory, fabrication, and characterization of solid state devices including P-N junctions, capacitors, bipolar and MOS devices. Devices are fabricated using modern VLSI processing techniques including lithography, oxidation, diffusion, and evaporation. Physics and performance of processing steps are discussed and analyzed.

nodes.title: Integrated Circuit Design and Fabrication
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Either ECE 120A or ECE 124B with a minimum grade of C- or better in each of the courses.
nodes.description: Design, simulation, fabrication, and characterization of NMOS integrated circuits. Circuit design and layout is performed using commercial layout software. Circuits are fabricated using modern VLSI processing techniques. Circuit and discrete device electrical performance are analyzed.

nodes.title: VLSI Principles
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 152A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Introduction to CMOS digital VLSI design: CMOS devices and manufacturing technology; transistor level design of static and dynamic logic gates and components and interconnections; circuit characterization: delay, noise margins, and power dissipation; combinational and sequential circuits; arithmetic operations and memories.

nodes.title: VLSI Architecture and Design
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 124A or ECE 123 or ECE 122A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Practical issues in VLSI circuit design, pad/pin limitations, clocking and interfacing standards, electrical packaging for high-speed and high-performance design. On-chip noise and crosstalk, clock and power distribution, architectural and circuit design constraints, interconnection limits and transmission line effects.

groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives

nodes.title: Signal Analysis and Processing
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B or 5A with a minimum of grade of C; open to EE and computer engineering majors only.

items.text: 5A with a minimum of
open to EE and computer engineering majors only

nodes.description: Analysis of continuous time linear systems in the time and frequency domains. Superposition and convolution. Bilateral and unilateral Laplace transforms. Fourier series and Fourier transforms. Filtering, modulation, and feedback.

nodes.title: Signal Analysis and Processing
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 130A with a minimum grade of C- or better; open to EE and computer engineering majors only.

items.text: open to EE and computer engineering majors only

nodes.description: Analysis of discrete time linear systems in the time and frequency domains. Z transforms, Discrete Fourier transforms. Sampling and aliasing.

nodes.title: Introduction to Applied Linear Algebra
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Math 4B or Math 5A recommended. Open to EE and CE majors only.

items.text: MATH 4B or MATH 5A recommended
Open to EE and CE majors only

nodes.description: Introduction to applied linear algebra: matrix arithmetic, vector spaces, orthogonality, matrix factorizations, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, difference and differential equations.

nodes.title: Introduction to Solid-State Electronic Devices
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 4 or 24 or 7D with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 4B, 4BI or 5A with a minimum grade of C; open to EE and computer engineering majors only.

items.text: open to EE and computer engineering majors only

nodes.description: Electrons and holes in semiconductors; doping (P and N); state occupation statistics, transport properties of electrons and holes; P-N junction diodes; I-V, C-V, and switching properties of P-N junctions; introduction of bipolar transitors, MOSFET's and JFET's.

nodes.title: Introduction to Optimization and Learning
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Upper division standing Electrical Engineering and Computer Engineering majors only.

items.text: Upper division standing
Electrical Engineering and Computer Engineering majors only

nodes.description: Includes an undergraduate level introduction to the theory of optimization, along with relevant applications of optimization in machine learning and statistics, signal processing, decision making and control.

nodes.title: Introduction to Fields and Waves
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 3 or 23 or 7B and Physics 4 or 24 or PHYS 7C with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 4B or 4BI or 5A and Mathematics 5B or 6A or 6AI with a minimum grade of C in each; and Mathematics 5C or 6B with a minimum grade of C-; open to EE and computer engineering majors only.

items.text: open to EE and computer engineering majors only

nodes.description: Introduction to applied electromagnetics and wave phenomena in high frequency electron circuits and systems. Waves on transmission-lines, elements of electrostatics and magnetostatics and applications, plane waves, examples and applications to RF, microwave, and optical systems.

nodes.title: Optical Fiber Communications
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 132 and 134 with a minimum grade of C- in both.
nodes.description: Optical fiber as a transmission medium, dispersion and nonlinear effects in fiber transmission, fiber and semiconductor optical amplifiers and lasers, optical modulators, photo detectors, optical receivers, wavelength division multiplexing components, optical filters, basic transmission system analysis and design.

nodes.title: Introduction to Optics and Photonics
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: PHYS 5/PHYS 5L or PHYS 7D/PHYS 7L or PHYS 25 or equivalent.

items.text: equivalent

nodes.description: Fundamentals of optical and photonics including lens theory, basics of imaging, microscopes and telescopes, 2-dimensional Fourier Transforms, optical coherence, interferometry, lasers, laser phase noise and laser linewidth.

nodes.title: Optics and Imaging
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: PHYS 5/PHYS 5L or PHYS 7D/PHYS 7L or PHYS 25 or equivalent.

items.text: equivalent

nodes.description: Photonics, with an emphasis on imaging: optical design (Zemax), ray transfer matrices, aberrations, scattering, resolution and optical transfer functions, adaptive optics, polarization, laser scanning, ultrafast pulses, detectors, superresolution, and VR/AR.

nodes.title: Quantum Photonics
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: PHYS 5/PHYS 5L or PHYS 7D/PHYS 7L or PHYS 25 or equivalent.

items.text: equivalent

nodes.description: Introduction to quantum information, fundamentals of quantum photonics, quantum light generation and detection, quantum coherence and superposition, wave-particle duality, qubits, quantum logic, entanglement, quantum measurement.

nodes.title: Circuits and Electronics I
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 10A-B-C and 10AL-BL-CL or 2A-B-C, 130A and 132 all with a minimum grade of C-; open to EE majors only.

items.text: open to EE majors only

nodes.description: Analysis and design of single stage and multistage transistor circuits including biasing, gain, impedances and maximum signal levels.

nodes.title: Circuits and Electronics II
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 10C and 10CL or 2C, and ECE 137A with a minimum grade of C- in all; open to EE majors only.

items.text: open to EE majors only

nodes.description: Analysis and design of single stage and multistage transistor circuits at low and high frequencies. Transient response. Analysis and design of feedback circuits. Stability criteria.

nodes.title: Probability and Statistics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: Open to Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering and pre-Computer Engineering majors only.

requires.text: Open to Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering and pre-Computer Engineering majors only

nodes.description: Fundamentals of probability, conditional probability, Bayes rule, random variables, functions of random variables, expectation and high-order moments, Markov chains, hypothesis testing.

nodes.title: Introduction to Nanoelectromechanical and Microelectromechanical systems (NEMS/MEMS)
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ME 16 or ME W 16 and 17; ME 152A and ME 151A (may be concurrent); or ECE 130A & 137A with a minimum grade of C- in both.
nodes.description: Introduction to nano- and microtechnology. Scaling laws and nanoscale physics are stressed. Individual subjects at the nanoscale including materials, mechanics, photonics, electronics, and fluidics will be described, with an emphasis on differences of behavior at the nanoscale and real-world examples.

nodes.title: MEMS: Processing and Device Characterization
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ME 141A or ECE 141A.
nodes.description: Lectures and laboratory on semiconductor-based processing for MEMS. Description of key equipment and characterization tools used for MEMS and design, fabrication, characterization and testing of MEMS. Emphasis on current MEMS devices including accelerometers, comb drives, micro-reactors and capacitor-actuators.

nodes.title: INTRODUCTION TO POWER ELECTRONICS
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 132, ECE 134 and ECE 137A with a minimum grade of C- in all; open to EE majors only.

items.text: open to EE majors only

nodes.description: An introduction to modern switched-mode power electronics and associated devices. Covers modern converter/inverter topologies for the control and conversion of electrical power with high efficiency with applications in power supplies, renewable energy systems, lighting, electric/hybrid vehicles, and motor drivers.

nodes.title: Electromagnetic Fields and Waves
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 134 with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Waves on transmission lines, Maxwell's equations, skin effect, propagation and reflection of electromagnetic waves, microwave integrated circuit principles, metal and dielectric waveguides, resonant cavities, antennas. Microwave and optical device examples and experiencewith modern microwave and CAD software.

nodes.title: Communication Electronics
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 137A-B with a minimum grade of C- in both.
nodes.description: RF/Microwave circuits. Transistor, transmission-line, and passive element characteristics. Transmission-line theory and impedance matching. Amplifier design for maximum available gain. Amplifier stability. Gain compression and power limits. Introduction to noise figure, and to intermodulation distortion.

nodes.title: Communication Electronics II
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 145A with a minimum grade of C-; EE majors only.

items.text: EE majors only

nodes.description: RF models for CMOS and BJT. Discrete vs. IC implementation. On-chip passive components. LNAs. PAs. T/R switches. Mixers. VCOs. Poly-phase filters Radio link budget. Analog and digital modulation schemes. Introduction to receiver architectures. I&Q modulation. Image-reject architectures.

nodes.title: Communication Electronics III
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 145B with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Modern wireless communication standards. Cellular phone. Wireless LAN. Introduction to multi-access techniques. Advanced modulation schemes. Interference and distortion. Modern transceiver architectures. Direct conversion vs. low IF vs. super-heterodyne. Sub-sampling receiver. Direct polar modulator. Frequency synthesis using PLL.

nodes.title: Digital Communication Fundamentals
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 130A-B with a minimum grade of C-; ECE 139 or PSTAT 120A; open to CE & EE majors only.

items.text: open to CE  and  EE majors only

nodes.description: Signal and channel models, with emphasis on wireless systems; digital modulation; demodulation basics; statistical modeling of noise, including review of probability theory and random variables.

nodes.title: Advanced Topics in Wireless Systems
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 146A with a minimum grade of C- or better; open to EE and CE majors only.

items.text: open to EE and CE majors only

nodes.description: A selection of topics in advanced wireless communication and sensing systems, including multi-antenna (MIMO) and multicarrier (OFDM) systems, and wideband MIMO radar.

nodes.title: Feedback Control Systems - Theory and Design
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 130A-B with a minimum grade of C- in each; open to electrical engineering and computer engineering majors only.

items.text: open to electrical engineering and computer engineering majors only

nodes.description: Feedback systems design, specifications in time and frequency domains. Analysis and synthesis of closed loope systems. Computer aided analysis anddesign.

nodes.title: Digital Control Systems - Theory and Design
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 147A with a minimum grade of C-; open to EE and CE majors only.

items.text: open to EE and CE majors only

nodes.description: Analysis of sampled data feedback systems; state space description of linear systems: observability, controllability, pole assignment, state feedback, observers. Design of digital control systems.

nodes.title: Control System Design Project
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 147A or ME 155B or ME 173 with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Students are required to design, implement, and document a significant control systems project. The project is implemented in hardware or in high-fidelity numerical simulators. Lectures and laboratories cover special topics related to the practical implementation of control systems.

nodes.title: Applications of Signal Analysis and Processing
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 130A and 130B with a minimum grade of C- in both.
nodes.description: A sequence of engineering applications of signal analysis and processing techniques; in communications, image processing, analog and digital filter design, signal detection and parameter estimation, holography and tomography, Fourier optics, and microwave and acoustic sensing.

nodes.title: Game Theory for Networked Systems
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: UPPER DIVISION STANDING OR CONSENT OF INSTRUCTOR.

items.text: UPPER DIVISION STANDING
CONSENT OF INSTRUCTOR

nodes.description: An overview of game theory with an emphasis on application to multiagent systems. Game theory focuses on the study of systems that are comprised of interacting and possibly competing decision-making entities. Examples drawn from engineered, economics, and social systems.

nodes.title: Digital Design Principles
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 15A and ECE 2A or ECE 10A & ECE 10AL with a minimum grade of C- in each course; or Computer Science 30 or 64 with a minimum grade of C- in each course; open to electrical engineering, computer engineering, and computer science majors only.

items.text: open to electrical engineering, computer engineering, and computer science majors only

nodes.description: Design of synchronous digital systems: timing diagrams, propagation delay, latches and flip-flops, shift registers and counters, Mealy/Moore finite state machines, Verilog, 2-phase clocking, timing analysis, CMOS implementation, S-RAM, RAM-based designs, ASM charts, state minimization.

nodes.title: Digital System Design
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 152A with a minimum grade of C-; open to EE, CMPEN, and Computer Science majors only.

items.text: open to EE, CMPEN, and Computer Science majors only

nodes.description: Hierarchical digital design both top-down and bottom-up with special emphasis on the role of wire loading, architecture design with partitioning, planning, and timing closure. Module and system interfaces and communication structural design. Design debugging using on chip JTAG based resources, static timing analysis, multiple clock domains, synchronization and computer peripheral design.

nodes.title: Hardware/Software Interface
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Upper division standing in Computer Engineering, Computer Science and Electrical Engineering. Familiarity with C, FiniteAutomata, and Computer Architecture.

items.text: Upper division standing
Computer Science

nodes.description: Design and coding of embedded programs. Real-time constraints and management of resources. Practical I/O interfaces and protocols, polling, interrupt maintenance, atomic code, blocking and non-blocking tasks. Static and dynamic task scheduling under real-time and limited resource constraints.

nodes.title: Sensor and Peripheral Interface Design
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 152A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Hardware description languages; field-programmable logic and ASIC design techniques. Mixed-signal techniques: A/D and D/A converter interfaces; video and audio signal acquisition, processing and generation, communication and network interfaces.

nodes.title: Introduction to Computer Architecture
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 152A with a minimum grade of C-; open to EE and CMPEN majors only.

items.text: open to EE and CMPEN majors only

nodes.description: Instruction-set architecture (ISA) and computer performance; Machine instructions, assembly, addressing modes; Memory map,arrays, pointers; Procedure calls; Number formats; Simple ALUs; Data path,control, microprogram; Buses, I/O programming, interrupts; Pipelined data paths and control schemes.

nodes.title: Advanced Computer Architecture
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 154A with a C- grade or better. Open to EE and CMPEN majors only.

items.text: Open to EE and CMPEN majors only

nodes.description: ISA variations; Pipeline data and controlhazards; Fast ALU design; Instruction-level parallelism, multithreading, VLIW; Vector and array processing, multi/many-core chips; Cache and virtual memory; Disk arrays; Shared- and distributed-memory systems, supercomputers; Reconfigurable and application-specific circuits.

nodes.title: Machine Learning in Design and Test Automation
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 152A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Introduces the various machine learning techniques and how they are utilized to improve hardware design and test automation processes. The potential benefits and theoretical barriers for implementing a machine learning solution in practice are explained.

nodes.title: Artificial Intelligence in Design and Test Automation
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 157A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Introduces an artificial intelligence system view to apply machine learning in design and test automation processes. The various components for building an Intelligent Engineering Assistant (IEA) to perform an engineering task in an industrial setting are explained.

nodes.title: AI Agents for the Semiconductor Industry
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; open to Computer Engineering and Electrical Engineering Majors.

items.text: Upper-division standing
open to Computer Engineering and Electrical Engineering Majors

nodes.description: Covers theories and practices of verification/test for checking hardware correctness and trustworthiness of large language models. A connection between the two is drawn. Students learn the principles of verification and test and how to apply them in both contexts.

nodes.title: Digital Signal Processing
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives

nodes.description: Electrons as particles and waves, Schrodinger's equation and illustrative solutions. Tunnelling. Atomic structure, the exclusion principle and the periodic table. Bonds. Free electrons in metals, periodic potentials and energy bands.

nodes.title: Optoelectronic Materials and Devices
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 162A-B with a minimum grade of C-; open to electrical engineering and materials majors only.

items.text: open to electrical engineering and materials majors only

nodes.description: Optical transitions in solids. Direct and indirect gap semiconductors. Luminescence. Excitons and photons. Fundamentals of optoelectronic devices: semiconductor lasers, Led's photoconductors, solar cells, photo diodes, modulators. Photoemission. Integrated circuits.

nodes.title: Introduction to Digital Image and Video Processing
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Open to electrical engineering, computer engineering, and computer science majors with upper-division standing.

items.text: Open to electrical engineering, computer engineering, and computer science majors with
upper-division standing

nodes.description: Basic concepts in image and video processing. Topics include image formation and sampling, image transforms, image enhancement, and image and video compression including JPEG and MPEG coding standards.

nodes.title: Introduction to Robotics: Dynamics and Control
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 130A or ME 103
nodes.description: Dynamic modeling and control methods for robotic systems. Lagrangian method for deriving equations of motion, introduction to the Jacobian, and modeling and control of forces and contact dynamics at a robotic end effector. Laboratories encourage a problem-solving approach to control.

nodes.title: Introduction to Robotics: Planning and Kinematics
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4A and Upper-Division standing only.

items.text: Upper-Division standing only

nodes.description: Motion planning and kinematics topics with an emphasis on geometric reasoning, programming, and matrix computations. Motion planning: configuration spaces, sensor-based planning, decomposition and sampling methods, and advanced planning algorithms. Kinematics: reference frames, rotations and displacements, kinematic motion models.

nodes.title: INTRODUCTION TO DEEP LEARNING
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Open to EE, Computer Engineering and Computer Science with upper-division standing.

items.text: Open to EE, Computer Engineering and Computer Science with
upper-division standing

nodes.description: Introduction to multilayered neural networks, early models of perceptrons and associative memory; back-propagation learning; convolutional neural networks; recurrent neural networks; attention models; applications to natural language processing and computer vision.

nodes.title: Introduction to Computer Vision
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing in Artificial Intelligence, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Chemical Engineering or Mechanical Engineering.

items.text: Upper-division standing
Electrical Engineering

nodes.description: Overview of computer vision problems and techniques for analyzing the content of images and video. Topics include image formation, edge detection, image segmentation, pattern recognition, texture analysis, optical flow, stereo vision, shape representation and recovery techniques, issues in object recognition, and case studies of practical vision systems.

nodes.title: Nonlinear Phenomena
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 105A or Physics 103; or ME 163 or upper-division standing in ECE.

items.text: upper-division standing

nodes.description: Introduction to nonlinear phenomena. Flows and bifurcations in one and two dimensions, chaos, fractals, strange attractors. Applications to physics, engineering, chemistry, and biology.

nodes.title: Introduction to Video Game Development
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: CS 130A and CS 130B or significant programming experience in large software systems.

items.text: significant programming experience in large software systems

nodes.description: Introduction to game design, video game architectures, large-scale software design patterns, game aesthetics, user interface design, and playtesting, all within the Unity3D framework. Quarter culminates in a high-quality video game suitable for public release. Pre-requisite for the advanced game-development sequence.

nodes.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 139 or PSTAT 120A or equivalent.

items.text: equivalent

nodes.description: An introductory course to topics in machine learning studied from a probability theory viewpoint. Covers an overview of basic probability, inference and estimation, regression algorithms, Markov chains, inference for Markov models and the EM algorithm, Markov decision process, and reinforcement learning. In addition to covering mathematical and algorithmic details, the course includes several hands-on projects to implement the machine learning algorithms.

nodes.description: Student groups design a significant project based on the knowledge and skills acquired in earlier coursework and integrate their technical knowledge through a practical design experience. The project is evaluated through written reports, oral presentations, and demonstrations of performance.

nodes.description: General philosophy of programming and problem-solving. Students will be introduced to the programming language MATLAB. Specific areas of study will include algorithms, basic decision structures, arrays, matrices, and graphing.

groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Upper-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Senior standing in engineering.
nodes.description: The nature of moral value, normative judgment and moral reasoning. Theories of moral value. The engineer's role in society. Ethics in professional practice. Safety, risk, responsibility. Morality and career choice. Code of ethics. Case studies facilitate the comprehension of the concepts introduced.

nodes.title: Introduction to Programming
nodes.description: General philosophy of programming and problem-solving. Students will be introduced to the programming language MATLAB. Specific areas of study will include algorithms, basic decision structures, arrays, matrices, and graphing.

nodes.title: Calculus with Algebra and Trigonometry
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam.

requires.text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam

nodes.description: Math 3A with precalculus: A function approach integrating algebra, trigonometry, and differential calculus. Topics include: one-on-one and onto functions; inverse functions; properties and graphs of polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions; properties and graphs of trigonometric functions; analytic geometry; functions and limits; derivatives; techniques and applications of differentiation; introduction to integration; logarithmic and trigonometric functions.

nodes.title: Calculus with Algebra and Trigonometry
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Math 3B with precalculus: A continued review of relevant topics from precalculus (see Math 2A); integral calculus, including definite and indefinite integrals; techniques of integration, introduction to sequences and series; with applications in mathematics and physics.

nodes.title: Calculus with Applications, First Course
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam.

requires.text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam

nodes.description: Differential Calculus including analytic geometry, functions and limits, derivatives, techniques and applications of differentiation; introduction to integration; logarithmic and trigonometric functions.

nodes.title: Calculus with Applications, Second Course
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 3A with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Integral calculus including definite and indefinite integrals, techniques of integration; introduction to sequences and series; with applications in mathematics and physics.

nodes.title: Linear Algebra with Applications
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: Math 2B or 3B or 3BI with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Systems of linear equations, matrix algebra, determinants, vector spaces and subspaces, basis and dimension, linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalization, and orthogonality.

nodes.title: Differential Equations
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: Math 4A or Math 4AI with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: First and second order differential equations, separation of variables, linear differential equations, systems of first order equations, nonlinear differential equations and stability.

nodes.title: Vector Calculus with Applications, First Course
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4A (or 4AI) with a letter grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Calculus of functions of several variables, vector valued functions of one variable, derivative and integrals of vector functions, double and triple integrals, properties and applications of integrals, change of variables.

nodes.title: Vector calculus with Applications, Second Course
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Preparation
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B (or 4BI) and Mathematics 6A, each with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Scalar and vector fields, integration along paths, integration over surfaces and solid regions, integral theorems of vector calculus, Fourier series, partial differential equations.

nodes.title: Transition to Higher Mathematics
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4A or 4AI or 4B or 4BI or 6A or 6B with a grade of B or better.
nodes.description: Introduction to the elements of propositional logic, techniques of mathematical proof, and fundamental mathematical structures, including sets, functions, relations, and other topics as time permits. Mastery of this material is essential for students planning to major in mathematics.

nodes.title: Structure and Properties I
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 1A-B and Mathematics 4B, 6A, 6B
nodes.description: An introduction to materials in modern technology. The internal structure of materials and its underlying principles: bonding, spatial organization of atoms and molecules, structural defects. Electricial, magnetic and optical properties of materials, and their relationship with structure.

nodes.title: Structures and Properties II
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Materials 100A.
nodes.description: Mechanical properties of engineering materials and their relationship to bonding and structure. Elastic, flow, and fracture behavior; time dependent deformation and failure. Stiffening, strengthening, and toughening mechanisms. Thermo-mechanical interactions in materials.

nodes.title: Fundamentals of Structural Evolution
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Materials 100A and Materials 100B.
nodes.description: An introduction to the thermodynamic and kinetic principles governing structural evolution in materials. Phase equilibria, diffusion and structural transformations. Metastable structures in materials. Self-assembling systems. Structural control through processing and/ or imposed fields. Environmental effects on structure and properties.

nodes.title: Introduction to the Structure and Properties of Materials
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.description: Introduction to the structure of engineering materials and its relationship with their mechanical properties. Structure of solids and defects. Concepts of microstructure and origins. Elastic, plastic flow and fracture properties. Mechanisms of deformation and failure. Stiffening, strengthening, and toughening mechanisms.

nodes.description: Introduction to applied mechanics. Forces, moments, couples, and resultants; vector algebra; construction of free body diagrams; equilibrium in 2- and 3-dimensions; analysis of frames, machines, trusses and beams; distributed forces; friction.

nodes.title: Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 7A or Physics 2, and ME 14 with a minimum grade of C-, and Math 6B or Math 5C (may be taken concurrently); open to ME majors only.

items.text: open to ME majors only

nodes.description: Vectorial kinematics of particles. Coordinate systems, moving frames, relative and constrained motion. Dynamics of particles and systems of particles. Energy and momentum methods. Collisions. Planar kinematics and kinematics of rigid bodies. Energy and momentum methods for rigid body systems.

nodes.title: Mathematics of Engineering
nodes.prereq_text: Engineering 3; open to ME majors only.

items.text: open to ME majors only

nodes.description: Introduction to basic numerical and analytical methods, with implementation using MATLAB. Topics include a Matlab review, ordinary differential equations, partial differential equations and boundary conditions, eigenvalue/eigenvectors. Graphic and visualization tools in Matlab.

nodes.title: Dynamical Systems
nodes.prereq_text: Math 6B and ME 16
nodes.description: Equations of Motion for Mechanical, Electrical, Heat, Fluid, and Control Systems. Block diagram algebra and interconnections. Laplace transform. Transfer functions and dynamic stability. First and second order systems. Frequency response. Introduction to mechanical vibrations and feedback control design.

nodes.title: Introduction to Nanoelectromechanical and Microelectromechanical systems (NEMS/MEMS)
nodes.prereq_text: ME 16 or ME W 16 and 17; ME 152A and ME 151A (may be concurrent); or ECE 130A & 137A with a minimum grade of C- in both.
nodes.description: Introduction to nano- and microtechnology. Scaling laws and nanoscale physics are stressed. Individual subjects at the nanoscale including materials, mechanics, photonics, electronics, and fluidics will be described, with an emphasis on differences of behavior at the nanoscale and real-world examples.

nodes.title: Thermosciences 1
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 7D or Physics 2, and ME 14 with a minimum grade of C-, and Math 6B or Math 5C
nodes.description: Basic concepts in thermodynamics, system analysis, energy, thermodynamic laws, and cycles.

nodes.title: Fluid Mechanics
nodes.prereq_text: Math 6B or Math 5C, and ME 16 or ME W 16 with a minimum grade of C-, and Physics 7B or Physics 2
nodes.description: Introduction to the fundamental concepts in fluid mechanics and basic fluid properties. Basic equations of fluid flow. Dimensional analysis and similitude. Hydrodynamics.

nodes.title: Control System Design
nodes.prereq_text: ME 17 with a minimum grade of C-; ME 103.
nodes.description: The discipline of control and its application. Dynamics and feedback. The mathematical models: transfer functions and state space descriptions. Simple control design (PID). Assessment of a control problem, specification, fundamental limitations, codesign of system and control.

nodes.title: Advanced Control Systems Design
nodes.prereq_text: ME 155A.
nodes.description: Dynamic system modeling using state-space methods, controllability and observability, state-space methods for control design including pole placement, and linear quadratic regulator methods. Observers and observer-based feedback controllers. Sampled-data and digital control. Laboratory exercises using MATLAB for simulation and control design.

nodes.title: Engineering Mechanics: Vibrations
nodes.prereq_text: ME 16 or ME W 16 with a minimum grade of C-; ME 103; open to ME majors only.

items.text: open to ME majors only

nodes.description: Topics relating to vibration in mechanical systems; exact and approximate methods of analysis, matrix methods, generalized coordinates and Lagrange's equations, applications of systems. Basic feedback systems and controlled dynamic behavior.

Measurement, units, and foundations of physics; vectors; kinematics; circular motion; forces, mass, and Newton's laws; center of mass; momentum; work and energy; conservation laws; collisions; rotational kinematics.

Unit circle and trigonometric identities. Polar coordinates and kinematics in polar coordinates.

nodes.title: Fundamentals of Business Strategy
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Sophomore standing or higher.
nodes.description: An introduction to business strategy, principles and practices required for business success in the competitive market place. Students are exposed to key management theories, models and tools including competitive strategy, finance, planning, new product development, marketing, leadership and others.

nodes.title: Entrepreneurship
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Departmental Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Sophomore standing or higher.
nodes.description: Learn how to start any type of venture; for profit, non-profit, service, sole-proprietorship, with a focus on high-tech ventures. Analysis of new business opportunities, development of customer-centric value propositions, financing, marketing, selling, and protection of intellectual property.
